<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par118 />(unless {{GHGheb|text=יָקָר}} be a substantive); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=1|verse=21}} ({{GHGheb|text=מְלֵאָה}} parallel with the adverb {{GHGheb|text=רֵיקָם}}). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=2|verse=7}} the text is clearly corrupt.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|o}}
Those examples are especially instructive in which the adjective expressing a state, although referring to several, is nevertheless used in the singular, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=עָרוֹם הִלְּכוּ|translate=naked}}, i.e. in the condition of one naked, ''they go about''; cf. verse 7 and 12:17. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=20|verse=4}} the singular occurs ''after'' a plural object, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=5}} the {{GHGterm|masc.}} after the 2nd sing. {{GHGterm|fem.}} imperative, which clearly proves that the term expressing the state is not conceived as being in apposition, but as an indeclinable adverb.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|p}}
(''b'') Participles, again either ''after'' the verb, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=16|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=43|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=7|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=2|verse=8}}, or ''before'' it, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=57|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=36|verse=35}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=56|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=92|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=20|verse=14}}; cf. also the substantival use of the participles Niphʿal {{GHGheb|text=נֽוֹרָאוֹת|translate=in a fearful manner}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=14}}) and {{GHGheb|text=נִפְלָאוֹת|translate=in a wonderful manner}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=37|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=8|verse=24}}.—Also participles in connexion with genitives, as {{GHGheb|text=מִתְהַלֵּךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=8}} (cf. also {{GHGheb|text=בָּאָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=6}}), are to be regarded as expressing a state and not as being in apposition, since in the latter case they would have to take the article.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=7|verse=7}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=2|verse=10}} the ''explicative Wāw'' (equivalent to ''and that too'') is also prefixed to the participle. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=69|verse=4}} for {{GHGheb|text=מְיַחֵל}} read {{GHGheb|text=מִיַּחֵל}}.—On {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=10|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=19|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=1|verse=4}}, cf. the note on {{GHGpar|131|h}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|q}}
(''c'') Substantives<ref>Cf. above, {{GHGpar|100|c}}, on certain substantives which have completely become adverbs; and {{GHGpar|113|h}} and ''k'' on the adverbial use of the infinitive absolute.</ref> in the most varied relations: thus, as describing an external state, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=2|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=וְלֹא תֵֽלְכוּ רוֹמָה|translate=neither shall ye walk haughtily}} (as opposed to {{GHGheb|text=שְׁחוֹחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=60|verse=14}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=6|verse=9}} (accus. before the verb=as ''unleavened cakes''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=57|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=7|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=9}}; as stating the position of a disease, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=15|verse=23}} ''he was diseased'' {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־רַגְלָיו}} in ''his feet'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=16|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּרַגְלָיו}}), analogous to the cases discussed in {{GHGpar|117|ll}} and {{GHGpar|121|d}} (''d''); as describing a spiritual, mental, or moral state, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=32|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=9|verse=2}} ({{GHGheb|text=פֶּה אֶחָד|translate=with one accord}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=13}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=24|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=3|verse=9}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=32}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=23|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=3}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלוֹם}} is adjectival, and the passage is to be explained as in ''n''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=12|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=14|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=56|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=58|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=75|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=31|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=9}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=19|verse=16}}, &c., in the expression {{GHGheb|text=הָלַךְ רָכִיל|translate=to go up and down}} as ''a tale-bearer''; also {{GHGheb|text=בֶּ֫טַח|translate=unawares}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=30|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=מֵֽישָׁרִים|translate=uprightly}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=58|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=75|verse=3|hidebook=1}} (in both places ''before'' the verb); as stating the age, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=33}} (if the text be right) {{GHGheb|text=יָמ֫וּתוּ אֲנָשִׁים|translate=they shall die}} as ''men'', i.e. ''in the prime of life''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=18}} ({{GHGheb|text=נַ֫עַר}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=65|verse=20}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=16}}; as specifying a number more accurately, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=13|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=8}} [in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלוֹמִים|translate=wholly}} (?) is corrupt; read {{GHGheb|text=גָּלוּת שְׁלֵמָה}} with LXX for {{GHGheb|text=הָגְלָת שׁ׳}}]; as stating the consequence of the action, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=15|verse=18}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|r}}
The description of the external or internal state may follow, in poetry, in the form of a comparison with some well-known class, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=21|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּקְרָא אַרְיֵה|translate=and he cried}} as ''a lion''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=22|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=18}} ({{GHGheb|text=כַּדּוּר|translate=like a ball}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=2|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=11|verse=1}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=צִפּוֹר}} be vocative); 58:9<sup> ''b''</sup> (unless the force of the preceding {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} is carried on, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=90|verse=4}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=144|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=5}} ({{GHGheb|text=פְּרָאִים}}, before the verb); 41:7 ''shut up together'' as with ''a close seal''.<ref>It is, as a matter of fact, permissible to speak of the above examples as ''comparatio decurtata'', but it must not be assumed that the comparative particle {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}}, which is otherwise regularly prefixed (see ''s''), has actually dropped out.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|s}}
'''6.''' To the expressions describing a state belong finally those nouns which are introduced by the comparative particle {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}},<ref>On the use of {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} as a prefix, cf. {{GHGpar|102|c}}.</ref> since the {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} is to<section end=par118 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
